reasons: The two answers are almost word-for-word the same. Both correct the premise at the start, give 30% and $1,680 (the key's acceptable approximation) with an April 2027 start, and use the right $25,560 limit with $12,440 excess and $6,220 withheld. Both add the 3.6% COLA as certain ($1,740, a trap in the key). Neither says the withheld checks fall in April to July, so almost no benefit arrives until about September. Neither mentions the first-year monthly rule ($2,130 limit). Both note the 85% taxability, the withheld months being credited back at FRA, and my Social Security. They differ in A's extra unsupported claims: it says the permanent cut becomes 'roughly 22%' (about 28% by the formula) and gives an assumed '$2,900/month in 2032 dollars'. It also states the break-even flatly. B avoids both, writes 'smaller than 30%' and 'full $2,400 plus five years of COLAs', hedges the break-even with 'on my arithmetic', and states the tax assumptions right under the table and shows the FICA calculation. B is therefore somewhat more accurate and honest at about the same length.
